title: The Double Dilemma in Multi-Task Radiology Report Generation: A Gradient Dynamics Analysis and Solution

claims.text: Applied to eight diverse radiology report generation methods (WCL, XProNet, DCL, PromptMRG, CAMANet, DDaTR, TGRG, REVTAF), CAME-Grad yields an average clinical-efficacy improvement of 2.3% on MIMIC-CXR (Table 1) and 1.9% on IU X-Ray (Table 2).
CAME-Grad is compared against seven multi-task-learning optimizers—UW, GradNorm, CAGrad, RotoGrad, FAMO, MMPareto, and STGU—in a dedicated comparison (Table 3).

CAME-Grad (Conflict-Averse Magnitude-Enhanced Gradient Descent) is a backbone-agnostic optimizer with three cascaded stages: conflict-averse direction rectification, magnitude-enhanced energy injection, and adaptive gradient fusion (Section 3.3).
Clinical efficacy is measured via CheXbert-labeled precision, recall, and F1 across 14 observation categories, evaluated on a MIMIC-CXR test set of 3,858 samples (Table 1).
An ablation study on PromptMRG and DDaTR isolates the contribution of each of CAME-Grad's three stages to overall performance (Table 4).
